column1: # Per-chromosome mappable fraction for copy-number estimation.
# Copy number is covered_bp / expected_bp. Taking expected_bp as the chromosome's
# full reference length assumes every base is reachable by the k-mer index, which
# is false: rDNA, satellite and other sequence that does not resolve to a single
# chromosome in a one-individual reference never gets counted. The acrocentrics
# lose 13-19% of their length that way, so a normal diploid chr21 measures ~1.6
# copies, not 2.0 -- and `round()` then reports monosomy whenever noise pushes it
# under 1.5. Two of 115 release-2 samples lost that coin flip (NA18940 chr21 at
# `factor` is the observed ratio divided by the sample's own median autosome
# ratio, so it is a property of the DATABASE (its k and feature set), not of any
# assembly. Dividing expected_bp by it restores a 2.0 scale and, unlike a
# dead-band around the rounding boundary, stays sensitive in BOTH directions: a
# real trisomy 21 measures ~2.4 raw, which is 3.0 once calibrated.
# Derived: median over 105 HPRC release-3 samples (the better assemblies), all
# with normal autosome complements, annotated with HKS_human_CHM13_v2 at k=31.
# 230 release-2 samples give the same values within 0.02 (chr21 0.809 vs 0.826,
# chr13 0.867 vs 0.869, chr9 0.915 vs 0.915) -- independent assembly generations
# agreeing is what shows the factor belongs to the database.
# chrX / chrY are absent on purpose: their expected copy number depends on sex,
# so they are never rescaled here. A chromosome missing from this file gets 1.0.
